2. Pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS; localized or diffuse) — strong possibility: recurrent, often painless monoarticular knee swelling in this age group; systemic labs often normal; MRI diagnostic.
3. Synovial hemangioma / intra‑articular vascular malformation — plausible: episodic painless swelling from intermittent bleeding/vascular engorgement, normal routine coagulation tests, identified by Doppler/contrast MRI.
4. Baker (popliteal) cyst secondary to intra‑articular pathology — likely as a cause of intermittent posterior knee swelling and commonly associated with underlying joint disease (including JIA); readily identified on ultrasound.
